content:
jamie: Quick sync — I ran the recurrence scan for the last 12 months and pulled incidents with 2+ repeats. Want to surface the top signatures, outstanding postmortem action gaps, and lock owners + deadlines for remediation. Summary below and proposed owners. Please ack and update if you own any items.

jamie: Top recurring signatures (count):
- cache-thrash during steady traffic (28)
- model OOMs on long-context requests (14)
- control-plane rollout timeouts (10)
- degraded routing after multiregion failover (6)

jamie: Notable remediation gaps:
- cache-thrash: several PMs recommended smarter prefix eviction + KV cache hygiene; only 1/4 actions completed.
- model OOMs: temporary mitigations (shorter max_len) were applied, but we never completed quantization/packer changes or single-request fallback.
- rollout timeouts: runbooks exist but no enforced canary gating; CD pipeline has no automatic rollback on increased p99.

jamie: Proposed owners & timelines (please confirm or reassign):
- cache-thrash -> sam (impl smarter prefix caching + hot-key autosuppress). target: 2026-05-30.
- model OOMs -> alex (quantization + controlled packing + fallback path). target: 2026-06-15.
- rollout timeouts -> maria (canary gating + auto-rollback policy). target: 2026-05-20.
- multiregion routing -> priya (post-failover validation suite + alerting). target: 2026-05-28.

sam: I can own cache-thrash. timeline looks ok but need 2w dedicated perf lab time and a couple GPUs for long-run tests. Will open a request to infra today.

alex: Taking model OOMs. Quick note: need access to the model packing repo and the eval prompts used in the PMs. Also propose a short-term runtime flag to limit context for large models during peak load while we ship quant changes.

maria: I'll pick up rollout canary gating. I want to prototype gate based on route-level p99 and error-rate, plus block merges that spike p99 > 2x baseline. Will coordinate with eng-platform for pipeline hooks.

priya: I'll own the multiregion validation suite and add the checks to the incident checklist. Also I can do the remediation board updates and track weekly progress. Will create a card per remediation item and set owners + dates.

oncall-bot: Reminder: recurring-incident-scan job runs every Monday at 07:00 UTC. Last run attached to this thread.

jamie: Action items:
- sam -> create design doc + infra ticket (due 2026-04-09).
- alex -> PR with quant plan + runtime flag proposal (draft by 2026-04-12).
- maria -> pipeline gating PR + runbook update (draft by 2026-04-08).
- priya -> remediation board cards + weekly cadence (board up by 2026-04-06).

priya: I'll add owners in the postmortem artifacts too and tag each PM original owner for visibility.

sam: quick Q: do we want to prioritize cache-thrash over canary gating? both are high but cache impacts customer latency more.

maria: my read — cache-thrash has higher user-facing impact and is inexpensive to prototype. prefer parallel work but prioritize tests for cache changes first.

alex: +1 to parallel but if infra slots limited, prioritize cache-thrash. quant work needs longer lead time.

jamie: Agreed — run cache-thrash work first for short-term wins, but keep model OOMs on fast-track (parallel docs + flag).

priya: I'll block weekly 30-min sync on Fridays starting next week to review progress and unblock owners.

jamie: Thanks all. Please update the remediation board and the postmortem entries by EOD Monday so I can compile status for the monthly ops review. If anything slips on timelines, ping me directly.

sam: Ack.

alex: Ack, starting repo access requests now.

maria: Ack — will have gating prototype by next week.

priya: Ack — board cards created, invites sent for Friday sync.
